messages.Albania: Albania commends Brazil and Switzerland for their tireless efforts as co-penholders to find common ground on this vital humanitarian file. In line with the unequivocal call of the Secretary-General and humanitarian organizations on the ground, we maintain that a full 12-month renewal is essential to ensure operational predictability and adequate winter planning for millions of vulnerable Syrians. While we recognize that nine months is already a substantial compromise to bridge council divisions, we strongly encourage keeping the mandate duration aligned with genuine humanitarian needs.
messages.China: China appreciates the efforts of Brazil and Switzerland as co-penholders to find common ground. However, humanitarian assistance must fully respect Syria's sovereignty and government ownership, with cross-border aid remaining strictly temporary while cross-line relief is prioritized. To achieve consensus and reflect the legitimate concerns of all parties, the mandate should be renewed for six months, and the detrimental impact of unilateral sanctions on humanitarian relief must be explicitly addressed.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador fully supports the draft resolution prepared by co-penholders Brazil and Switzerland, which represents a balanced and vital compromise to preserve life-saving assistance. The nine-month renewal of the cross-border mechanism at Bab al-Hawa is essential to ensure operational predictability and address the dire humanitarian needs of millions of civilians in north-western Syria, particularly following the devastating earthquakes. We urge all Council members to prioritize humanitarian imperatives and consensus to ensure this vital lifeline remains open.
messages.France: France thanks Brazil and Switzerland for their tireless dedication in drafting this text to preserve the cross-border humanitarian lifeline. In line with the unequivocal appeals of the Secretary-General and humanitarian organizations on the ground, France strongly advocates for a 12-month renewal to provide predictable planning and uninterrupted aid through the harsh winter months. While France remains committed to constructive engagement to avoid any disruption to the mechanism, we urge the penholders to maintain the push for a full one-year mandate.
messages.Gabon: Gabon commends the co-penholders, Brazil and Switzerland, for their tireless efforts to craft a balanced compromise with this nine-month renewal. In light of the critical humanitarian needs of the Syrian people, further exacerbated by the devastating February earthquakes, the Security Council must preserve this vital humanitarian lifeline while continuing to expand cross-line deliveries and early recovery projects. We urge all Council members to demonstrate flexibility and consensus to avoid any disruption to life-saving assistance.
messages.Ghana: Ghana commends the co-penholders, Brazil and Switzerland, for their tireless efforts to bridge differences and put forward this pragmatic compromise draft. The cross-border mechanism remains an indispensable lifeline for millions of vulnerable civilians in north-western Syria, particularly in the wake of the devastating earthquakes. Ghana fully supports the proposed nine-month extension as a sensible middle ground ensuring predictability for humanitarian operations, and we urge all Council members to unite behind this text.
messages.Japan: Japan expresses its deep appreciation to Brazil and Switzerland for their tireless and balanced efforts as co-penholders to forge consensus on this vital humanitarian file. While Japan, along with the Secretary-General and humanitarian organizations, strongly favored a 12-month renewal to provide essential operational predictability, we fully support this 9-month compromise to ensure the cross-border lifeline at Bab al-Hawa remains open. We urge all Council members to put the humanitarian needs of the Syrian people first and unite behind this draft.
messages.Malta: Malta commends Brazil and Switzerland for their tireless efforts as co-penholders to maintain this vital humanitarian lifeline for millions of people in north-west Syria. In line with the unequivocal recommendation of the Secretary-General and humanitarian partners on the ground, Malta strongly advocates for a full 12-month extension to ensure predictability and sustained aid delivery through the upcoming winter. While we urge the Council to strive for a 12-month authorization, Malta remains constructive and committed to preserving Council unity to protect cross-border access.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique commends Brazil and Switzerland for their tireless engagement and balanced efforts to bridge divides on this vital humanitarian file. We support the proposed draft and the nine-month renewal of the Bab al-Hawa crossing as a sensible compromise that provides necessary operational predictability for humanitarian actors on the ground. We urge all Council members to maintain unity and flexibility so that lifesaving assistance reaches all Syrians in need without disruption.
messages.Russian Federation: The cross-border mechanism is an obsolete, temporary modality that infringes upon the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic and cannot continue indefinitely. We cannot accept a nine-month mandate; the only viable, balanced timeline is a six-month extension until 10 January 2024. If the co-penholders genuinely wish to preserve humanitarian assistance rather than engage in political posturing, they must adjust the duration to six months and reflect key realities, including the suffocating impact of unilateral coercive measures on ordinary Syrians.
messages.Switzerland: As co-penholder alongside Brazil, Switzerland fully supports this draft resolution. A nine-month renewal represents a carefully calibrated compromise designed to bridge differences in the Council while ensuring that the vital humanitarian lifeline through Bab al-Hawa remains open across the harsh winter months. We urge all Council members to unite behind this text to meet the pressing humanitarian needs of over four million people in north-west Syria.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates commends Brazil and Switzerland for their balanced compromise proposal that prioritizes the urgent humanitarian needs of the brotherly Syrian people. We strongly support expanding early recovery activities across all sectors, including electricity and humanitarian mine action, which is vital for the safety of civilians and the restoration of livelihoods. We urge all Council members to maintain unity and constructive engagement so that essential aid operations can continue uninterrupted.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom commends Brazil and Switzerland for their dedicated leadership as co-penholders. The Secretary-General and humanitarian organizations on the ground have been unequivocal that a full 12-month extension is essential to provide operational certainty and meet unprecedented humanitarian needs. While we appreciate the penholders' efforts to bridge differences, the Council must prioritize the humanitarian imperative and provide the certainty that 4.1 million Syrians desperately need.
messages.United States of America: The United States thanks Brazil and Switzerland for their dedicated leadership as penholders on this vital humanitarian file. The Secretary-General, UN agencies, and humanitarian partners on the ground have been unequivocal that a full 12-month renewal is the operational minimum needed to ensure predictable procurement, staffing, and life-saving assistance through the harsh winter. While we recognize the penholders' efforts to bridge divides, Council members must prioritize the clear humanitarian needs of over four million Syrians over political gamesmanship.

before.Brazil:
I have the honour to deliver this statement on behalf of Switzerland and my own country, Brazil, as co-penholders of the Syrian humanitarian file in the Security Council.

Over the past weeks, we have worked tirelessly and engaged extensively with all Council members, humanitarian actors on the ground, and key regional stakeholders to find common ground and preserve this vital humanitarian lifeline. The draft resolution before us today is the result of intensive consultations and represents a carefully crafted compromise.

Millions of people in north-western Syria rely on the cross-border mechanism authorized by this Council through the Bab al-Hawa crossing for their daily survival. The needs are greater than ever, aggravated by more than a decade of conflict, severe economic hardship, and the catastrophic consequences of the earthquakes that struck the region in February.

While the Secretary-General and the humanitarian community have clearly advocated for a 12-month extension to ensure predictability and continuity of operations, we have listened carefully to the concerns and different perspectives expressed across the Council. In that spirit of responsibility and compromise, we have proposed a nine-month extension until 10 April 2024. 

This draft also strongly underscores the importance of scaling up cross-line deliveries throughout the country and expanding early recovery projects, including in basic services, electricity, and humanitarian mine action, in line with United Nations humanitarian principles.

The cross-border operation remains irreplaceable at this stage. It is our collective duty as members of this Council to prioritize the lives and well-being of millions of vulnerable civilians who depend on our unity and action today. We therefore urge all members of the Council to vote in favour of this draft resolution.
before.Russian Federation:
(spoke in Russian): The Russian delegation will vote against the draft resolution submitted by the co-penholders, Brazil and Switzerland, contained in document S/2023/506. 

From the very beginning of the negotiations, we have consistently underscored that the cross-border mechanism for humanitarian deliveries is an obsolete, temporary arrangement that violates the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic. Over the past year, Western delegations have shown zero intention of genuinely advancing cross-line deliveries to north-west Syria, nor have they taken any concrete steps to lift the illegitimate unilateral sanctions that are suffocating the Syrian people and hindering early recovery projects.

We clearly stated that we could only consider an extension of the mechanism strictly for a period of six months, until 10 January 2024, coupled with clear demands regarding the development of cross-line access, early recovery, and addressing the impact of unilateral coercive measures. Instead of seeking a genuine compromise that respects Syrian sovereignty, the co-penholders and Western members chose to push forward an unacceptable nine-month proposal, completely disregarding our red lines. 

Russia has prepared its own draft resolution providing for a technical six-month extension of the cross-border mechanism, which fully addresses the genuine humanitarian needs of the population while respecting the sovereignty of Damascus. If our draft is not supported, the cross-border mechanism will simply cease to exist. The responsibility for the collapse of this mechanism lies squarely with our Western colleagues.

after.Albania:
I thank the co-penholders, Brazil and Switzerland, for their tireless efforts, dedication, and exhaustive consultations to reach a balanced and compromised text that had the overwhelming support of this Council. 

Albania voted in favour of the draft resolution because the cross-border mechanism is an indispensable, life-saving lifeline for over 4 million people in north-western Syria. After twelve years of brutal conflict, catastrophic economic collapse, and the devastating earthquakes of February, humanitarian needs in Syria are at their highest level ever. 

Today, thirteen members of this Council acted responsibly and in accordance with humanitarian imperatives. Yet, once again, a single permanent member chose isolation, cynicism, and obstruction by misusing the veto. This is not just a veto against a text; it is a veto against humanity, a veto against children, women, and families who rely on basic food, shelter, and medicine for their daily survival. 

Humanitarian assistance should never be politicized, nor should the lives of millions of vulnerable people be held hostage to narrow political calculations and geopolitical bargaining. There is simply no viable alternative to the Bab al-Hawa crossing at the scale and scope needed to address this ongoing catastrophe. 

Today is another dark day for the Security Council. By preventing the Council from fulfilling its basic humanitarian duty, the Russian Federation has dealt a severe blow to the Syrian people and to the credibility of this body. We deeply regret this reckless decision, which will undoubtedly have to be accounted for before the General Assembly. Albania remains firmly committed to the Syrian people and will continue to support every effort to ensure that life-saving humanitarian aid reaches all those in need without hindrance.

I thank you.
after.China:
(spoke in Chinese): China has always maintained that humanitarian assistance to Syria must be provided in a manner that fully respects Syria’s sovereignty and the ownership of the Syrian Government. Cross-line assistance should become the primary channel for humanitarian relief to Syria. The cross-border mechanism is a temporary arrangement made under specific circumstances, and it is necessary to accelerate the transition to cross-line relief and eventually phase out the cross-border mechanism.

China has consistently participated actively and constructively in the consultations on the draft resolution and commends the co-penholders, Brazil and Switzerland, for their tireless efforts to bridge differences and seek consensus. At the same time, we have always emphasized that Council members should resolve differences through patient and in-depth consultations. Forcing a vote when major differences still exist and parties are not yet aligned will only exacerbate divisions, undermine the unity of the Security Council, and do a disservice to resolving the problem. In view of that, China abstained from the vote on the draft resolution.

China calls on all Council members to keep the broader picture in mind, demonstrate maximum political will, accommodate each other’s legitimate concerns, continue consultations, and strive to reach a solution acceptable to all as soon as possible. Furthermore, we reiterate that unilateral coercive measures have severely compounded the humanitarian crisis in Syria, hindered the country’s economic recovery, and obstructed humanitarian operations and early recovery efforts. Those unilateral sanctions must be lifted immediately and completely.
after.France:
*(spoke in French)*

France deeply deplores the veto cast today by the Russian Federation. By opposing the compromise draft resolution prepared by Brazil and Switzerland, Russia has once again chosen to take millions of Syrian civilians hostage and to isolate itself from the rest of the Council.

The renewal of the United Nations cross-border humanitarian mechanism is a matter of absolute humanitarian necessity. More than four million people in north-western Syria depend on this vital lifeline for their survival, particularly in the aftermath of the devastating earthquakes of February. The Secretary-General, United Nations humanitarian agencies, and non-governmental organizations on the ground have all made clear that a 12-month renewal was indispensable to ensure predictability and continuity in aid delivery.

In a spirit of compromise and to respond to the urgent needs of the population, France voted in favour of the draft resolution proposed by the co-penholders for a renewal of nine months. This draft resolution was a balanced text that took into account the concerns of all parties, including early recovery projects and cross-line deliveries. Thirteen members of this Council supported it.

Yet, Russia chose cynically to block this compromise, as it has done repeatedly in the past, putting its political calculations above the basic needs of vulnerable populations.

France commends the tireless efforts of Brazil and Switzerland to achieve consensus, and we salute the dedication of humanitarian workers who continue their life-saving work under extremely perilous conditions. 

France’s position remains unchanged. We will continue, along with our partners, to support the Syrian people. But we reiterate that there can be neither normalization, nor financing of reconstruction, nor the lifting of sanctions until a credible and inclusive political process is firmly under way, in full accordance with resolution 2254 (2015).
after.Switzerland:
Switzerland deeply regrets that the Security Council was unable to adopt the draft resolution just voted upon, due to the veto cast by a permanent member. 

As co-penholders with Brazil, Switzerland has worked tirelessly over the past weeks to find a compromise that would bridge differing positions and respond to the immense humanitarian needs on the ground. The draft resolution presented today was the result of extensive, transparent, and inclusive consultations with all members of this Council, the United Nations humanitarian agencies, and regional partners. 

The cross-border humanitarian mechanism authorized by this Council is a matter of life and death for over 4 million people in north-west Syria. The needs are currently at their highest level since the beginning of the conflict, compounded by the catastrophic earthquakes of February. The Secretary-General, humanitarian organizations, and non-governmental organizations on the ground have consistently stated that there is simply no alternative to the cross-border mechanism at Bab al-Hawa that can match its scope, predictability, and efficiency. 

While the humanitarian community repeatedly called for a twelve-month extension to ensure predictability and planning for operations, particularly ahead of the harsh winter months, we proposed a nine-month extension as a viable, constructive compromise to accommodate the concerns of all Council members. 

Humanitarian aid should never be held hostage to politics. Today's outcome is a devastating blow to millions of civilians who depend on this Council to ensure that vital aid continues to reach them. 

Switzerland will not give up. We remain fully committed, alongside Brazil, to continuing our efforts to keep this essential humanitarian lifeline open. We urge all members of the Council to put the humanitarian imperative first and assume our shared responsibility towards the people of Syria.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
I thank the co-penholders, Brazil and Switzerland, for their tireless and principled efforts to find a compromise solution to maintain this vital humanitarian lifeline.

The United Kingdom voted in favour of the draft resolution because the humanitarian imperative is clear: 4.1 million people in north-western Syria depend on the United Nations cross-border mechanism for their survival. While the Secretary-General, United Nations humanitarian agencies, and non-governmental organizations on the ground were unequivocal in requesting a 12-month mandate—which is essential to provide operational certainty, particularly as winter approaches—the co-penholders put forward a compromise of nine months to accommodate the concerns of Council members.

Thirteen members of this Council voted for this compromise. Yet once again, Russia has chosen to use its veto to cut off a humanitarian lifeline for millions of vulnerable Syrian men, women, and children. There is no humanitarian justification for Russia’s veto today. It is an act of sheer cynicism and cruelty, holding life-saving assistance hostage to political leverage.

Cross-line aid, while welcome, cannot match the scale and scope of cross-border operations. Without the United Nations cross-border mechanism, the lives of millions are at immediate risk. 

The United Kingdom will not abandon the Syrian people. We will continue to work with our partners and the United Nations to explore all viable options to ensure that life-saving humanitarian assistance continues to reach those in desperate need.
after.United States of America:
This is a sad day for this Council, and a sad day for the Syrian people.

I am deeply, deeply disappointed that Russia has chosen to put its own cynical political interests ahead of the humanitarian needs of millions of vulnerable people. Just moments ago, 13 members of the Security Council voted in favour of a compromise text to extend the cross-border humanitarian mechanism through Bab al-Hawa for nine months. Thirteen of us voted to keep this vital humanitarian lifeline open because we listened to the Secretary-General, we listened to United Nations humanitarian agencies, we listened to non-governmental organizations on the ground, and we listened to the Syrian people themselves.

For millions of people in north-western Syria—people who have endured twelve years of war, poverty, disease, and the catastrophic devastation of February’s earthquakes—Bab al-Hawa is literally a lifeline. It is how food, clean water, hygiene kits, and life-saving medicines reach families who have nowhere else to turn.

The co-penholders, Brazil and Switzerland, worked tirelessly and in good faith to reach a consensus. The humanitarian community asked for a 12-month extension to ensure predictability and planning. In a spirit of compromise, the co-penholders proposed a nine-month extension to accommodate the concerns of Council members, including the Russian Federation. But Russia could not even accept this compromise. Instead, Russia chose to cast a veto.

Let us be completely clear about what just happened: Russia has once again held life-saving humanitarian assistance hostage. This is an act of utter cruelty. It is an unconscionable blow to millions of Syrians who rely on this aid for their daily survival.

Russia’s actions today demonstrate total disregard for the lives of the Syrian people and contempt for the humanitarian principles this Council is supposed to uphold. Russia has isolated itself, standing entirely alone against 13 members of this Council.

To the Syrian people, and to the humanitarian workers who risk their lives every single day to deliver aid: the United States stands with you. We will not give up. We will continue to explore every possible avenue to ensure that humanitarian assistance reaches those in desperate need, and we call on all members of this Council to redouble their efforts to ensure this vital lifeline remains open.
